newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir security forces punished for rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir security forces punished for rights abuses.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said 272 security personnel in the troubled Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir were punished for human rights violations in the past five years, local news agencies reported on Thursday.
"In keeping with our policy of transparency, this information has been widely reported," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Deve Gowda as saying.
Deve Gowda said the nation adhered to a transparent human rights policy, including regions where militant separatists were active, PTI reported.
Dozens of Kashmiri groups are fighting for independence or a merger with Pakistan in the disputed Himalayan state.
Police and hospital sources say at least 20,000 persons have been killed in a bloody separatist revolt since 1990.

"Such violations were committed by individual members of the security forces and were not reflective of any systemic failure as the forces were engaged in counter-insurgency operations to protect the unity and integrity of the country," the United News of India (UNI) quoted Deve Gowda as saying.
